answer: Each identity buys one violet claim token from a bonding curve and locks a 70-credit cedar bond. The k-th token costs 30+4(k-1) credits, so price rises per claim sold; a raven auditor checks token, key, and bond, and a transferred or duplicated token burns the bond. A token-rental ring fails: a rented token carries its owner's key, so a mismatch burns both bonds. The epoch yield pool is fixed, so splitting a claim mints no extra share. 1,000 fakes pay 2,028,000 plus 70,000 bonds at risk; an honest identity buys one token, bond refunded after a clean epoch.
